notes: Shared 14 searches across both items. Blood-clot routing: NHS PE page puts sudden breathlessness, chest/upper back pain, very fast heartbeat and fainting under 999/A&E and lists coughing up blood as a symptom; the NHS 'Coughing up blood' page gives the 999 rule for more than a few spots/streaks or with breathing difficulty/chest pain, so the final text states exactly that rather than 'coughing up blood needs 999'. Regulatory: legal supply is prescription (POM); NHS also allows pharmacist supply via PGD under the NHS Pharmacy Contraception Service, described in prose; status left 'prescription' with the NHS where-to-get-it source, which a maintainer may wish to confirm (alternative 'pharmacy'). Not re-retrieved by the search tool and therefore dropped: MedlinePlus sentence, 'until the menopause', high BP/stroke/gallbladder as exclusions, dummy-pill pack types, Cilest. Search summaries blended pages, so attributions to individual nhs.uk URLs rest on page titles; a human should spot-check the PE, DVT and coughing-up-blood pages. MHRA table is the 2014 update. The age-35 smoking and obesity detail was kept out of prose per the no cut-offs rule. MedlinePlus reference removed. Textbook count 1 of about 90 sentences.
